This PR lands the adjudication mechanism on trusted main only. It does not itself adjudicate PR #1287's stale COMMENTED review (PRR_kwDOPyIw988AAAABLPwIjQ, 29 commits behind #1287's current head) — that is an explicitly separate, HOLD-gated follow-up per the originating directive (POST_ADJUDICATION_TO_PR1287=HOLD), not performed as part of this proof.

Running `pytest tests/pr_steward/ -q .` (trailing dot / broadened rootdir) pulls in unrelated duplicate-basename test trees and fails at collection; this is a pre-existing repo-wide pytest-invocation hazard unrelated to this change, surfaced during the independent audit. The correct scoped invocation is `pytest tests/pr_steward/ -q`.

The dedup key for conflicting receipts is the raw comment body string (exact bytes). A trusted approver's receipt that is edited after posting (same GitHub comment id, different body on refetch) is evaluated against whatever body the harvest captured at run time; this mechanism does not track edit history, consistent with the rest of the classifier's real-time-snapshot design.

findings.title: Conflict-detection dedup keyed on parsed fields + adjudicator, not raw bytes
findings.body: Original _find_review_adjudication built its conflict-detection signature from (review_id, head_sha, disposition, reason, adjudicator). This let two receipts with different raw comment bytes but identical parsed fields wrongly dedupe as one (false clearance), and made two byte-identical receipts from two different trusted approvers wrongly conflict (false denial), contradicting the documented byte-identical-duplicates rule. Fixed in af145c4b1 by keying the dedup set on the raw comment body string and dropping adjudicator from the comparison. Covered by test_byte_identical_body_from_two_different_trusted_authors_is_not_a_conflict and test_same_parsed_fields_but_different_raw_bytes_is_a_conflict.
